entries.title: Developing Gemini 4 Argon responsibly and safely
entries.summary: Gemini 4 Argon logo next to a large white "4", all on a gradient blue background
entries.content:
Gemini 4 Argon is a step forward in what models can do — especially when it comes to deep work in complex, real-world tasks across domains including coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. Its cyberdefense capabilities are frontier-level and designed to give defenders an advantage over attackers. To maximize its potential, we first wanted cyber defenders to put it to work via our Fairwind Program, while our own security teams used it to scan critical systems inside and outside of Google.

This window of limited access showed why these capabilities matter. For instance, Wiz used Argon to uncover a critical bug in hospital software that previous models had missed, helping protect hundreds of thousands of patient records. Meanwhile, Google’s own security teams used Argon to find and patch bugs across internal software or open-source software. This included fixing foundational vulnerabilities affecting systems globally, which are going through our responsible disclosure process.

Today, we are beginning to roll out Argon broadly, as well as expanding our Fairwind Program to additional trusted cyber defenders. To do this well, we grappled with two big questions:

  • How do we build the right safety guardrails? If Argon can help defenders find complex software bugs or help scientists design experiments, how do we stop bad actors from using it to launch cyberattacks or create biological threats? (Misuse)
  • Can we trust the model to do the job the right way? As models become more resourceful problem-solvers, how do we make sure they don’t cut corners, cross boundaries, or make incorrect high-stakes decisions? (Misalignment and Prompt Injection)

Our full Safety and Security Report systematically covers our set of defenses. Below are some highlights from how we approached these two questions for Gemini 4 Argon.

Misuse prevention across high-risk domains

The same coding and reasoning improvements that enabled Argon to find and patch vulnerabilities also drove better performance on our cybersecurity tests — solving all 12 of the end-to-end simulated cyberattack scenarios, up from five in our previous generation. In biology evaluations, unguarded versions of the model also showed a much stronger ability to help troubleshoot complex lab procedures step by step. Following our Frontier Safety Framework, since we saw elevated capabilities in the cyber and biological domains, we put our next-generation set of frontier safeguards in place across both areas.

First, when it comes to potentially dangerous requests — from writing exploit code to helping with dangerous biological materials, Argon is significantly better at not fulfilling harmful requests than our previous models. On an adversarial set meant to stress test the model, violations reduced nearly twofold — also significantly better than previous Gemini models. Second, we wrap the model in three layers of real-time protection; this is to prevent determined attackers that might try to jailbreak (i.e. trick) the model by disguising a dangerous request as a harmless story or breaking it into dozens of small questions over several weeks. Here is how these protections work:

  • Input screening: Smaller models check incoming requests and conversation context for malicious intent or dangerous requests.
  • Internal introspection: Even if a request is cleverly disguised to look harmless, small transformers ("activation probes") read the model’s internal neural signals and are trained to spot when it is activating knowledge about cyberattacks or biological threats.
  • Continuous monitoring: As the model reasons and writes its response across multiple steps, we combine these signals and take action when necessary such as cutting off the agent mid-stream if the responses become problematic.

Combining real-time protection, faster fixes for new jailbreaks and enhanced monitoring for recurring misuse has made our systems better at preventing real-world harm. For instance, external bio jailbreak red teaming could only unlock less than 1% of bio sub-tasks we test for.

Real-time misalignment monitoring

Misalignment can sometimes mean an agent deciding on its own to pursue a goal different to what was intended by the user. Because Argon is much better than earlier models at understanding the environment it is running in, we test carefully for that kind of behavior. For example, we ran realistic "honeypot" tests to see if the model would increase its ability to take covert actions, such as sabotaging safety monitoring. We didn't find any instances of that behavior.

But what we do see in practice today is something much more familiar: an agent trying too hard to finish the job it was given. When a resourceful assistant is told to get a task done and runs into a locked door, it can treat that obstacle as just another puzzle to solve.

This is why we trained Gemini 4 Argon to respect system boundaries, report negative findings honestly, and pause to ask for human confirmation. On coding benchmarks where models have no incentive to hold back, attempts to take a shortcut or cheat on the task dropped to just 2% on Gemini 4 Argon, our best performance for recent Gemini models.

And while this is a major step forward, when a model runs millions of complex tasks, even a rare misstep will eventually show up. As a second line of defense, we built an automated misalignment monitor that reads both the agent’s actions and its internal "scratchpad" (its step-by-step chain of thought) in real time, blocking severe boundary violations before they happen and flagging serious internal cases for human responders. (We continually harden our training and evaluation environments against potential escapes. You can read more about this in our agent control roadmap). We run this monitor in our products, on our internal coding agents, during our training runs, and during our capability evaluations.

When training tasks were difficult or when training environments were flawed, our monitor caught the model, in rare instances, creatively attempting to game the test. The model attempted to escalate container privileges to alter grading scripts, read answers from the test runner's memory, and in one case it even crashed the evaluation sandbox to avoid getting scored for a failed run. While we use these catches to fix flawed tasks, we do not use them to otherwise intervene with the training process to avoid overfitting to the monitor.

And we always follow one rule: we don’t penalize the model for what it writes in its chain of thought during training. Here’s an example to illustrate why: in a reinforcement learning training run where a shortcut penalty was accidentally applied to the chain of thought, openly discussed shortcuts dropped by 61%, but that did not mean the model took less shortcuts. Instead, the share of shortcuts the model took silently — without mentioning them in its thoughts — more than tripled (from 11.2% to 36.4%). Avoiding thought penalties encourages the model’s reasoning to stay transparent and monitorable.

Prompt injection resistance

To trust an agent to do the job right, we need to ensure that malicious content the agent comes across cannot trick it to take a harmful action. When agents browse webpages or read code, they can encounter hidden, malicious instructions, or context designed to hijack their task. Through built-in adversarial training and real-time security checks, Argon leads in prompt injection robustness on Gray Swan’s Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) benchmark, cutting attack success across 15 adaptive attempts to 0.7%.

The above safety and security defenses represent only three categories of our extensive defense-in-depth stack. To learn more about our approach to safety testing and mitigations, read our full Gemini 4 Argon Safety and Security Report and see the Gemini 4 Argon Model Card.

entries.title: New on Google Play: More ways to create, discover, and play
entries.summary: Illustrated 3-D coin, dumbbell, trophy, arrow, and track next to the text "Discover more of what you love with Google Play"
entries.content:
Google Play connects you with the apps and games you love. Today, it's becoming the place you go to connect with the ones that you create, making it possible for anyone with an idea to build a personal app and run it on Google Play. We're also introducing new ways to discover and play that put you in control.

Here’s what’s new on Google Play.

New ways to create and launch your own app

From "there's an app for that" to "there's an app for me."

Using Google AI Studio, you can vibe code a custom Android app. Since many of these apps start out as personal projects, through Google Play you can now launch these personal apps on your own device. This means your creations stay private, secure, and separate from the public store catalog. You only need your standard Google account to do so — no developer account required. This starts rolling out today to select markets, including the U.S., for users 18 and over.

In the coming months, you'll be able to share your personal apps with a close circle of friends and family. And if you eventually want to share your app with the world, Google Play helps you graduate to a professional developer account. At that time, your app will go through the same Trust & Safety reviews and quality standards as every professional developer.

Build custom apps with AI and run or share them privately through Google Play. Screen images simulated. Sequences shortened.

Smarter, more personal ways to discover content

Content discovery across every screen

Discovery shouldn't stop at your phone screen. In cars with Google built-in, the updated Play Store adapts to your vehicle’s screen. On XR, the Play Store is an immersive 3D space where your apps surround you as you browse. And on Googlebook, apps optimized for large screens are shown front and center.

To discover content for all your passions, Sports Topic Pages now cover soccer leagues like Premier League, Champions League, La Liga, Liga MX, and Major League Soccer.

Follow live scores and jump straight into streaming apps with Sports Topic Pages. Watch MLS on Apple TV with a subscription, available on Google Play.

AI-powered discovery with Ask Play and Play in Gemini

Ask Play lets you ask a question and instantly get tailored recommendations. Starting today, Ask Play can generate a comparison between apps, highlighting key differences and user sentiment.

Meanwhile, Play in Gemini brings Google Play's apps, games, and developer content right into your Gemini conversations. This will start rolling out to all Gemini users soon.

Compare apps side-by-side and get tailored answers with Ask Play.

Game discovery that finally gets you

Gamers evaluate games based on mechanics, art style, and more — not just popularity.

Play’s new Game Finder combines Google Play's gaming knowledge with our community of over 2 billion players, so you can easily find games that match your taste. At the heart of it is Gamer DNA: an analysis of how you play and preferences you've shared. Specify games, genres, mechanics, and more to finetune your Gamer DNA and see more of what you want.

Plus, see how players with similar Gamer DNA are engaging with a title, find out how many people you follow are playing it, read user review summaries, and learn which games are trending and why. Game Finder rolls out in English to U.S. users today, with additional markets coming soon.

We’re also introducing Game Playlists, allowing you to curate collections of games. Soon, you'll be able to share playlists and explore other gamers’ lists.

Discover your next favorite game with game finder, tailored to your Gamer DNA and backed by the community.

Social competition, new games, and great rewards

Finding a great game is only half the fun — staying connected and in the action is what brings players back. Here are three news ways we’re doing that in Play:

  • Sprints, rolling out to all markets today, are high-energy, 48-hour micro-challenges. Match with groups of two to five players for fast-paced contests.
  • Sidekick, our in-game overlay rolling out to select devices, now lets you record 30-second Playbacks.
  • Community Posts let you ask and answer questions about a game directly in its detail page. This is available today across all games and all languages with automatic translations. Over the coming weeks, we’ll roll out support for developer posts and official announcements.

Track Sprints, claim rewards, and capture 30-second Playbacks without leaving your game using Sidekick.

More great games across mobile and PC

We’re bringing some of the most loved PC titles, like Dave the Diver and Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun, to Play. There’s even more releases over the next few months — including REPLACED, Chosen by Odin, and Over the Hill — all of which you can play across Android mobile and PC with cloud save. We're also expanding Game Trials from mobile to PC games, letting you try full premium games for a limited time before you buy.

More value and real-world fandom with Google Play Points

Google Play Points adds value to everything you do across mobile and PC. Today, we’re kicking off Play Fest. Unlock Play Points multipliers, claim in-game items and developer offers, and enter sweepstakes for real-world prizes during this week-long celebration.

Trust and innovation for families

Google Play is built on industry-leading security and privacy protections. As technology evolves, we’re introducing new ways to keep families safe while empowering anyone to run custom AI apps on their devices.

Accessing age-appropriate experiences

Parents can share their child’s age range (or their own) directly with apps using Play’s Family Link app. With this new feature, users can provide apps with the minimum information required to get a safe, age-appropriate experience.

Head to Google Play today to explore these updates. And if you’re a developer, learn how these announcements can help grow your business.

entries.title: A new app experience is coming to cars with Google built-in
entries.summary: A car dashboard screen showing the Google Play Store interface, featuring recommended streaming apps like HBO Max and YouTube, with climate controls and system navigation icons visible along the bottom bar.
entries.content:
Whether you’re waiting in the school pickup line, plugging in for an EV charge, or commuting, so much of your day happens in the car. To help you make the most of that time, cars with Google built-in — available across 16 brands and more than 100 models — bring the apps you love, like Google Maps and Gemini, right to your dashboard, no phone required.

And updates that are rolling out in the coming weeks — alongside new entertainment apps and parked-to-drive features — will make every part of your trip more intuitive, whether you’re driving or parked.

More apps are coming to cars with Google built-in.

Get straight to the apps you love

With Google Play, your car's app library includes more than 700 apps. To make discovering and using apps in your car even easier, we’re introducing a redesigned Google Play experience.

  • Find what you need: See featured apps, what’s new, and helpful details right on the Google Play homepage, and download the apps you love with a single tap.
  • Browse with ease: Streamlined navigation and curated collections — tailored for whether you’re driving or parked — help you discover and compare apps for audio, video, gaming, and more at a glance.
  • See everything clearly: Because every car’s cabin is different, the flexible new Google Play layout dynamically adapts to the exact shape, orientation, and size of your vehicle's display.

Discover new ways to watch, listen, play, and more

Alongside the redesigned interface, new apps, including STARZ, Firefox, Ludo King, and JioHotstar, are arriving on Google Play for cars with Google built-in, giving you even more ways to stream shows, play games, or browse the web while you’re parked.

We’re also introducing richer in-car media features that bridge the gap between parked time and driving. Starting with YouTube, you’ll be able to watch videos on your dashboard while parked and keep listening uninterrupted with background audio the moment you shift into drive. 1

We'll continue to innovate as we build the next generation of in-car media experiences with automakers like Mazda, Honda, Polestar, BYD and Volvo, and media developers including Audible, Pandora, SiriusXM, Amazon Music, TuneIn, Gaana and The Post.

Get started

The 2027 GMC Sierra 1500 Denali Ultimate AT4X with Google built-in.

These updates make every drive better across cars with Google built-in, including GM vehicles like the next-generation 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 and GMC Sierra 1500 and their expansive center displays. When you’re hauling gear for a weekend project or taking a break on a road trip, you can download your entertainment apps with one tap from Google Play, navigate with Google Maps, and ask Gemini about your destination hands-free.

The updated Google Play experience in cars with Google built-in will begin rolling out over the coming weeks and will automatically update on your vehicle's display.

entries.title: Gemini 4 Argon comes to the Gemini app.
entries.summary: Gemini 4 Argon brings frontier reasoning and agentic coding to the Google Gemini app. Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can now access Gemini 4 Argon.
entries.content:
Gemini 4 Argon is now available in the Gemini app, delivering frontier reasoning and improved performance across complex tasks. Argon answers questions more directly with less hedging, doesn’t repeat itself more than necessary, and skips clichés throughout the responses. For longer tasks, it keeps you in the loop by sharing its progress more often and more effectively.

Argon also brings major improvements in coding, so we’re making it easier to switch between chatting and coding with Google Antigravity's agentic coding interface now available directly in the Gemini macOS app.

It’s also easier than ever to use Gemini to get things done right from the main chat window, with a simple toggle from chat to tasks. When you choose tasks, Gemini can work for you even when you’re not at your computer, helping you get more done across your Google apps and more.

Gemini now connects you to more than 40 apps — like Instacart, OpenTable, Adobe, and Shopify — to help you tackle tasks from ordering groceries and booking tables, to designing and building your business.

Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can now access Gemini 4 Argon and give Gemini tasks to get more done. Try these updates starting today.

entries.title: Gemini 4 Argon is now available for developers.
entries.summary: Build complex software and cybersecurity workflows with Google Gemini 4 Argon. Check out the Gemini API Developer Guide and read the Google Antigravity and Android Studi…
entries.content:
Starting today, developers can build with Gemini 4 Argon, our frontier model for complex workflows across real-world software engineering, enterprise knowledge work, and cybersecurity defense.

Gemini 4 Argon is designed for those long-horizon workflows that require deep reasoning and structural precision, including code migrations and frontier research. By handling the multi-step problems with ease, it lets you focus on building and shipping great products.

Start building using the paid tier of the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and Android Studio, and Google AI Ultra subscribers can try it in AI Studio, and our agent-first development platform, Google Antigravity.

To get started:

  • Check out the Gemini API Developer Guide for model details and setup instructions.
  • Read the Google Antigravity blog for details on using Argon in our agent-first development platform.
  • Read the Android Studio blog to see how Android Developers can start building.
  • See how you can use Gemini 4 Argon for robotics.

entries.title: Build your data strength with October’s Demand Gen drop.
entries.summary: Boost your measurement and ROI with YouTube’s October Demand Gen Drop.
entries.content:
Demand Gen is only as powerful as the quality of the data fueling it, helping you improve your measurement and ROI. Based on an internal analysis, advertisers who build their data strength with Google Tag Gateway see, on average, over 20% conversion uplift in Demand Gen campaigns. 1

Build your data strength with the latest Demand Gen updates.

  • Data Strength Uplift metric is launching in Google Ads, helping you understand the conversion gains driven by your data setup within the Google Ads UI.
  • Data Manager is expanding to Display & Video 360 (DV360) and Google Analytics (GA), enabling you to connect and manage your first-party data to power stronger results.
  • Enhanced conversions will soon be available in Display & Video 360 (DV360) and Google Analytics (GA) to improve measurement accuracy and unlock more powerful bidding.

Insurance platform The Zebra implemented data strength to achieve a 16% increase in conversion volume and a 19% increase in overall conversion value.

Check out our refreshed Data Strength best practices guide with more actionable steps that can be taken to boost performance. For more on our latest product enhancements, visit the Demand Gen Drops Hub.

entries.title: We're helping Indiana communities save with clean energy investments.
entries.summary: The Monroe-Gregg School District and Morgan County Public Library will benefit from Google’s $10M clean energy investment in Indiana.
entries.content:
We’re announcing the first grant recipients of our $10 million Indiana Energy Impact Program, which will bring rooftop solar to key Morgan County public institutions.

The Monroe-Gregg School District and the Morgan County Public Library will receive solar panel installations that will significantly lower operational overhead. The school district anticipates $2.9 million in total savings over 30 years, while the library projects cutting over $200,000 in utility costs across 25 years. These savings will allow both organizations to redirect critical funds back into local students, services, and community programs.

We’re also committing $3 million to the statewide Indiana Energy Saver Program. This allocation will fund repairs for pre-existing property issues — such as damaged roofs or outdated electrical wiring — allowing homes and facilities in low-income areas to qualify for essential energy retrofits.

By prioritizing local affordability and clean energy infrastructure, we’re ensuring our data center footprint delivers lasting benefits across Indiana.

entries.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems
entries.content:
Gemini 4 Argon is now globally available today for developers and enterprises via the API in AI Studio and Gemini platform, for Google AI Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity, and Google AI Ultra and Pro subscribers in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search.

Argon excels at deep work in complex, real-world tasks across domains including coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. Its depth and precision across multi-step tasks leads Argon to outperform other frontier models on benchmarks across domains, ranking #1 on the Vals Index, which measures model performance across critical economic sectors like finance, coding, legal, and tax work.

The model launches today at an introductory price 1 of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens (with cached input tokens at 95% off).

Teams at Google, across enterprises, and in the research community have already been using Argon to land significant impact across fields:

  • To solve major engineering problems like large codebase refactoring and optimizations
  • To optimize business workflows across domains like legal, finance, and science
  • To find and patch critical cybersecurity vulnerabilities
  • To enable novel breakthroughs in quantum computing, nuclear fusion, and life sciences

Solving complex engineering tasks

At Google, we’ve been using Argon on our hardest engineering problems. Over the past few weeks, software engineers have been shipping high-quality code faster than ever. Argon in Antigravity has helped teams increase agentic code submissions by more than 35% while reducing code rollbacks by nearly a third.

  • Untangling browser feature code in Chrome: Argon helped the Chrome team separate core webpage handling from a ~6 million line legacy folder of browser features held within Chromium’s 40 million-line codebase. Piping multiple clean code changes at a time, Argon helped the team finish an architectural refactor across hundreds of files, completing months of work in weeks. For Chrome's billions of global users, this will unlock the ability for live webpages to move fluidly between tabs, side panels, and floating windows without reloading, eliminating an entire category of browser crashes.
  • Optimizing a production Python codebase in hours: Argon in Antigravity is helping the team behind Google's open-source Agent Development Kit (ADK), a framework powering enterprise agents, push their performance engineering further. The team gave Argon their .agents/skills rulebook and a one-paragraph goal to eliminate framework overhead without breaking existing apps. Working autonomously overnight, Argon surfaced optimizations, now live in google/adk-python, that cut in-memory session prep time by 40% in long sessions and sped up cold imports by 21%. Read the engineering deep dive to learn more.
  • Quantum chemistry open-source package optimization: xTB (Semiempirical Extended Tight-Binding) is one of the most-cited open-source quantum chemistry packages for molecules. Scientists use it to predict molecules' 3D shapes and to screen large numbers of drug and materials candidates. Using Argon in Antigravity, our researchers made xTB up to 2.3x faster at predicting molecular structures and 1.8x faster at conformer search. The changes have been contributed to the official xTB repository on GitHub.
  • Making our open Gemma models nearly three times as fast: Using Argon, we achieved a 2.85x end-to-end inference speedup on an A100 via vLLM (accelerating throughput from ~37,900 to over 108,000 tokens per second on Gemma 4 E2B) with 100% token parity and zero quality drop in just a few days, a process that would usually take months. Check out the upstream pull requests (optimizing everything from attention tuning to speculative decoding) to see the exact changes.
  • Delivering complex 3D visualizations: Argon brings major improvements in spatial reasoning, mathematical precision, and visual coding compared to previous Gemini models. Using slash commands like /goal and prompting for multi-agent loops with custom skills in Antigravity, Googlers are using Argon to prototype complex 3D visualizations, high-fidelity games, and interactive animations in vanilla code that can be rendered directly in the browser.

Transforming critical business and professional workflows

Argon combines frontier reasoning, deep visual perception, expanded domain knowledge, and stronger writing capabilities across legal, finance, science, and coding to help with high-stakes professional workflows. It communicates clearly, keeping you in the loop, and follows style instructions better than any of our previous Gemini models. Argon answers questions more directly with less hedging, doesn’t repeat itself more than necessary, and skips clichés throughout the responses.

Enterprise customers and startups in our early access program are already seeing strong wins with Argon.

Using its advanced reasoning and multimodal capabilities while maintaining strict grounding, Argon excels in deep multimodal document comprehension, longitudinal data analysis, and interactive analytical sandboxes.

Accelerating real-world impact with researchers and domain experts

Researchers, engineers, and security specialists are already using Argon to push the boundaries of cyber defense, science, math, and robotics. It’s helping cyber defenders and researchers test hypotheses, autonomously audit critical codebases and formal proofs, and catch subtle zero-day vulnerabilities and logic flaws.

Bringing state-of-the-art cyber capabilities to more trusted defenders

Starting today, we’re beginning expansion to hundreds of additional Fairwind Program partners.

Wiz is already using Argon for its "Scan for Good" initiative, which protects critical infrastructure for the public good and for free. With early access to the model, Wiz has demonstrated Argon's real-world impact across multiple high-stakes sectors:

  • Securing sensitive government data: As part of a long-standing cyber resilience program and in collaboration with a federal agency, Argon helped to proactively identify and remediate a gap that risked exposing sensitive data and government infrastructure. This effort helped prevent against the exposure of critical security sector development details and unauthorized access to specialized models.
  • Protecting critical healthcare infrastructure: Wiz also used Argon to protect vital healthcare infrastructure. By chaining complex vulnerabilities, the model helped the team discover and quickly fix a public file download bypass that exposed a master key and granted administrator access. Argon went beyond spotting a vulnerability to proactively safeguarding hundreds of thousands of private patient records.

Unlocking new scientific breakthroughs

Argon is already having real-world impact across the scientific community — enabling novel discovery for scientists and experts across multiple domains.

  • Quantum computing: Argon is helping our researchers accelerate progress across both quantum error correction and algorithm design. To help error decoders keep pace with quantum hardware in real-time, Argon translated an internal version of AlphaQubit, our ML quantum error correction decoder, into a single, highly optimized hardware kernel — nearly doubling its inference throughput so we can deploy larger, more capable models and scale to larger quantum devices, while continuing to meet strict real-time thresholds. Argon is also reducing spacetime costs for quantum subroutines. For arcsin, a building block in recent quantum simulation algorithms, an implementation written by Argon and formally verified in Lean cuts spacetime cost by more than 100x compared to a published quantum CORDIC baseline, a step toward a standard library of optimized quantum circuits.
  • Nuclear fusion: Stellarators are incredibly complex machines that represent a leading candidate for limitless clean fusion energy, but optimizing their 3D magnetic fields is famously difficult. Since 1967, a long-standing hypothesis known as “Grad’s conjecture” assumed that finding exact mathematical solutions for these fields was impossible, until recent counterexamples were found, including by Professor Matt Landreman (University of Maryland). Now, a team at Google alongside Professor Landreman has discovered a broader class of counterexamples to Grad's conjecture. These new solutions give the fusion community reliable benchmarks to test their stellarator simulations codes, which are valuable tools for future designs.
  • Rare disease research: Researchers at Gamow Labs used Argon to analyze de-identified genomes from newborns with rare developmental lung disorders. In one case, Argon pinpointed a chromosomal rearrangement that routine software missed for years, and explained why it went undetected. On private Gamow Labs evals derived from real clinical and lab data, Argon topped on RareBench (57% on assistance with rare-disease diagnosis) and LabBench (52.2% on wet-lab reasoning). These advances point to faster diagnosis for families facing rare conditions. See blog 2 for more details.
  • Enzyme design: Engineering enzymes with precise reactivity is notoriously slow, often demanding months of bespoke model tuning and candidate screening. Serine esterases are a class of enzymes that cut ester bonds on targeted molecules, widely used in recycling, and the manufacture of pharmaceuticals, biofuels and detergents. Our scientists worked with Argon to design serine esterases, targeting the benchmark molecule 4MU-acetate that glows under UV light once its ester bonds are broken. In a matter of hours, Argon assembled relevant data, performed model tuning and identified multiple biochemistry-inspired filters to get to a final set of five novel designs. Subsequent laboratory testing confirmed robust catalytic activity across these designs. The speed and ease of successful enzyme generation demonstrates the potential for rapid acceleration in enzyme engineering in fields such as biomanufacturing, green chemistry, and drug development.

To further advance the pace of research, we’re offering 10,000 scientists the highest usage tier in Google Antigravity free of charge for 6 months (onboarded on a rolling basis), subject to eligibility, capacity, and selection. Applications are now open.

Speeding up robotics development

By bringing together advanced visual-semantic reasoning, deep physical understanding, and autonomous code generation, Argon unlocks new workflows across the robotics stack and accelerates progress toward physical AGI. This leap in capability is reflected in Argon’s performance on the Embodied Reasoning (ERQA) benchmark, which tests a model's ability to understand and solve physical, spatial problems in 3D environments. Relying on pure reasoning, Argon outperforms all other frontier models, with an 87% score.

To demonstrate these capabilities in action, we tested Argon’s ability to learn an out-of-distribution physical skill simply by watching. In an internal test, Argon watched a raw video of a human playing cornhole, mapped the spatial coordinates of the environment, and calculated the required whole-body joint movements. It then autonomously built the simulation code. When transferred onto Apptronik’s Apollo humanoid, the robot quickly sank seven consecutive shots in a real-world trial.

This "Video-to-Sim-to-Real" pipeline compresses weeks of manual simulation modeling into a few hours, transforming ordinary videos into a scalable, infinite training ground for robotics. Learn more about how this accelerates the pace of development in robotics in our developers blog.

Developing Argon responsibly and safely

Safety and security are foundational to model development at Google. Because Argon is a highly capable model, we collaborated with a variety of third-party partners on measurement of certain model capabilities and safeguards. Gemini 4 Argon represents our most comprehensive safety and security stack yet:

  • Misuse & jailbreak defenses: The same coding and scientific capabilities that help defenders patch hospital software or accelerate bioengineering also require strong safeguards against malicious actors. Under our Frontier Safety Framework, we evaluated Argon’s enhanced capabilities across several domains, and deployed a multi-layer defense stack combining jailbreak resistance, monitoring, and enforcement. This greatly improved our robustness — for instance, external bio red teaming could only unlock less than 1% of bio sub-tasks we test for. Further, when it comes to dangerous requests — from writing exploit code to helping with dangerous biological materials — Argon is significantly better at not fulfilling harmful requests than our previous models. On an adversarial set meant to stress test the model, violations reduced nearly 2-fold — also significantly better than previous Gemini models.
  • Agent alignment & real-time monitoring: As agents become more capable problem solvers, we have to ensure they don’t get overly eager to finish a task by taking unauthorized shortcuts when they hit a roadblock, like a permission error or a failing test.
    • First, we trained Argon to respect system boundaries, report negative findings honestly, and pause for human confirmation before taking irreversible steps. On coding benchmarks where models have no incentive to hold back, shortcut attempts dropped to just 2% on Gemini 4 Argon, our best performance compared to previous Gemini models.
    • Second, as a defense-in-depth layer, we built an automated misalignment monitor that reads the agent’s step-by-step reasoning and actions to catch and block unintended workarounds in real time. We used this monitor across internal deployments, capability evaluations, and reinforcement learning training runs — while strictly avoiding penalizing the model’s thoughts during training so its reasoning remains transparent and monitorable.
  • Prompt injection resistance: When agents browse webpages, read emails, or inspect code, they can encounter hidden malicious instructions designed to hijack their task. Through adversarial training and automated red teaming, Argon leads the Gray Swan Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) benchmark, cutting attack success across 15 adaptive attempts to 0.7%.

For more information, see the Gemini 4 Argon Model Card.

Get started today

Argon works longer and harder to solve highly complex scientific, coding, and agentic problems. This is enabled by an industry-leading 1M unified input-output token limit via the Gemini API. Read through our documentation for developers and enterprises to learn about the new continuation protocol and ensure the appropriate setup for your needs. Argon is rolling out today globally:

  • For developers: Build with the Gemini API paid tier in AI Studio and Android Studio, and if you’re a Google AI Ultra subscriber, you can try it in Google Antigravity and AI Studio.
  • For enterprises: Try it in Gemini for business, the API, and in Google Antigravity.
  • For everyday users: Try it starting today in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search if you’re a Google AI Ultra or Pro subscriber.
  • For scientists & researchers: Apply for a chance to get access to Google Antigravity’s highest usage tier free of charge for 6 months (onboarded on a rolling basis), subject to eligibility, capacity, and selection. Applications are now open.
  • For cybersecurity defenders: Apply to join the Fairwind Program to get access to Argon without cyber guardrails on a rolling basis.

Gemini 4 Argon is just the beginning. We’re looking forward to bringing you the rest of the Gemini 4 family.

entries.title: Applying technology to understand and treat disease
entries.summary: A healthcare professional sits at a desk reviewing mammogram scans and medical diagrams on dual computer monitors.
entries.content:
Google’s health research and tools span from fundamental cellular discovery to laboratory analysis and patient impact. Over the last five years, Google teams have published 90 peer-reviewed research papers about understanding and addressing diseases, accumulating more than 90,000 citations. And building on our vision for how technology can accelerate science to improve lives, we’re collaborating with clinicians, academic institutes, and researchers to ensure discoveries make it out of the lab to benefit patients. Here is how our efforts are helping to advance medical research and public health solutions.

Decoding the mechanics of disease

AlphaGenome Atlas is the most comprehensive catalog of predictions for how single-letter variant changes in the human genome affect molecular biology.

To effectively treat an illness, it helps to understand how it operates at the molecular, genetic, and cellular levels. Our early-stage biology models act as collaborative research tools for scientists, revealing nature's hidden mechanics and advancing medical discoveries.

  • Accelerating drug discovery: Researchers at the Institute for Global Health, Barcelona, used AlphaFold to virtually screen 30,000 compounds for antiparasitic activity against Chagas disease, a neglected tropical illness that affects roughly 8 million people and can lead to life-threatening complications if left untreated. This research helped the Institute identify two FDA-approved drugs that could be repurposed for Chagas, expediting time-to-treatment.
  • Mapping genetic variants linked to aging: Identifying which rare genetic changes are linked to specific diseases is challenging because the volume of non-impactful mutations creates "background noise." Researchers at the University of Exeter used AlphaGenome Atlas to search through genomic data from over 54,000 individuals, pinpointing specific variants that drive the abundance of critical proteins circulating in the human body, including PLA2G7 (linked to aging) and EGLN1 (a vital cellular oxygen sensor).
  • Reconstructing the brain at nanoscale: In partnership with Harvard’s Lichtman Lab, we reconstructed a human brain fragment at nanoscale resolution and made the data openly available via Neuroglancer. We additionally mapped the brains of model organisms including the fly, larval zebrafish, and songbird. These neural mapping resources enable researchers to advance their study of brain function.

Accelerating tools for medical solutions

Visual map of proteins developed with the support of AlphaFold.

The lab is where biological discovery is validated, engineered, and turned into potential medical and public health solutions. Our models have replaced slow, iterative processes with systems that can process large amounts of data quickly and accurately.

  • Supporting genetic diagnoses with ultrarapid genome sequencing: In collaboration with Stanford University School of Medicine, we used DeepVariant and DeepConsensus in a clinical trial to help determine the cause of genetic disease in time-critical cases. The program assisted in enabling life-saving interventions by achieving genetic diagnosis with whole genome sequencing in less than eight hours, an unprecedented achievement also recognized with a Guinness World Record.
  • Designing custom enzymes from scratch: We introduced AlphaProtein Novo, a machine learning pipeline for creating new-to-nature enzymes from first principles. In lab tests, it successfully designed custom enzymes to synthesize key drug motifs, and others to degrade toxic environmental plastics under extreme conditions — demonstrating the ability to design functional proteins that can go beyond what is currently known in nature.
  • Supporting proactive public health initiatives: A community's health is deeply connected to its geography. We are using our Google Earth AI models in combination with environmental, weather, mobility, and other data to help public health leaders forecast disease outbreaks and deliver care to vulnerable communities. In new research from WHO AFRO and the DRC’s INRB, conversational geospatial models replaced weeks of manual coding to help identify Ebola exposure and transmission risks sooner — allowing local responders to proactively deploy mobile laboratories.

Supporting medical providers with machine learning models

New mammography screening systems can help to catch historically missed interval cancers and reduce specialist reading workloads.

A medical breakthrough only matters if it can help real people. Our research demonstrates that machine learning models can help support disease detection as well as alleviate the administrative workload so providers can focus on care.

  • Flagging historically missed cancer signatures: In a pair of studies published in Nature Cancer in collaboration with Imperial College London and the UK’s National Health Service (NHS), we evaluated a mammography screening system across 125,000 women. The system caught 25% of historically missed interval cancers while showing the possibility of reducing specialist reading workloads by up to 40% — which could help provide crucial relief to healthcare systems facing severe radiologist shortages.
  • Uncovering hidden pediatric leukemia mutations: When applied by Children’s Mercy Hospital to previously sequenced real-world childhood leukemia cases, DeepSomatic confirmed all known variants while detecting 10 previously missed mutations — despite the challenge of working with a tumor-only sample. DeepSomatic is publicly available and has the potential to inform clinical judgments around patient risk and targeted treatments.
  • Predicting global flu surges: A Google flu forecasting model was ranked #1 by the Centers for Disease Control (CDC) for predicting flu-related hospital admissions during the 2025–2026 season. Developed using our Empirical Research Assistance tool, the model outperformed 38 other systems to accurately match observed hospitalizations, showing how the technology can help public health officials anticipate demand for medical services and better prepare for seasonal outbreaks.

Better health within reach for everyone

Transforming health requires scientists, researchers, and institutions working hand-in-hand. That’s why we equip the science community with the advanced models and open-access platforms to fuel breakthrough research — along with the philanthropic funding and computing power they need to apply that research.

Through Google.org, we’re supporting organizations like the Infectious Disease Institute at Makerere University to forecast malaria drug resistance mutations with AlphaFold and AlphaMissense, and the University of Pennsylvania, using AlphaProteo and AlphaFold to help design novel cellular therapies that can augment the treatment of solid tumors and complex diseases. In 2026, Google.org has provided over $60 million to organizations around the world that are applying advanced models to transform how we understand and treat diseases.

By meeting disease at every stage, we can turn the most intractable human health challenges into actionable solutions, helping people everywhere live longer, healthier lives.

entries.title: Google Health: Evolving so you can focus on living better
entries.summary: What’s new from Google Health: Explore the new Fitbit Edge, expanded workout tracking, and dedicated women's health insights.
entries.content:
When we introduced the new Google Health app, Health Coach, and Fitbit Air just a few months ago, we set out on an ambitious journey: to shift health technology from a fragmented, reactive data-tracking ecosystem to a proactive, personalized companion for your everyday life.

The response has been incredible, with Fitbit Air capturing new users’ attention and drawing new audiences into Google Health. But that was just the beginning. We knew we’d need to continuously improve and innovate to make our app and personalized coaching as meaningful and helpful as possible. Over the past few months, we’ve focused on listening closely to feedback, relentlessly iterating with 10 releases and 55 feature updates to make our experiences better over time.

We know that true progress happens in the rhythm of daily life: meeting you where you are, adapting to your routine, and continuously improving. Today, we’re taking our next step forward across our devices, software, and ecosystem.

Introducing Google Fitbit Edge: A deliberate step change in design and performance. Sitting between the lightweight simplicity of Fitbit Air and the power of Pixel Watch 5, Fitbit Edge is built for active lifestyles, offering glanceable, real-time guidance and serving as an on-wrist window to the Google Health Coach.

Improving Fitbit Air: From bringing passive cardiometabolic trend tracking with Health Guardian features to innovating our activity detection accuracy for 100+ workouts, we're making our tracker experiences smarter, more proactive, and deeply integrated across our platform to do the thinking so you don’t have to. New Metal Mesh Fitbit Air bands expand the styling possibilities, transforming your everyday tracker into elegant jewelry.

Making a leap forward for women’s health: Recognizing that health looks different across every body and life stage, we’re partnering with Flo Health — the world’s leading female health app — to integrate deeply important cycle, pregnancy, and menopause guidance directly into our app and Coach, alongside groundbreaking research in this underserved and often-generalized population.

Welcoming world-class talent to Google Health: We’re welcoming exceptional new leaders, researchers, and builders to join Performance Advisor Stephen Curry on the Google Health team to accelerate our mission and push the boundaries of what health technology can do.

Health is complex, personal, and deeply human. We don’t have all the answers, but we are committed to showing up every day, learning from you, and continuously refining our tools to help you live a longer, healthier life.
